title: Status of Fine Particulate Matter in B.C.
summary: Explore fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) management levels across seven B.C. air zones and the 57 monitoring stations assessed for 2022–2024.
sourceNote: This project preserves the air-zone geometries, station locations, management levels, and click details embedded in Environmental Reporting BC's June 2026 interactive map. The air zones were not previously present in BC Data Mapper, so they are now stored there once as a reusable boundary layer. Results reflect the 2022–2024 Canadian Ambient Air Quality Standards assessment and include approved adjustments for transboundary flows and exceptional events where the indicator applies them.
details: Click or tap an air zone or monitoring station for the metrics and assessment details supplied by the Province.
Fine particulate matter is PM₂.₅: airborne particles 2.5 micrometres or smaller that can penetrate deep into the lungs.
Management levels progress from keeping clean areas clean through preventing deterioration or exceedance to actions for achieving the standards.

scenes.label: Assessment
scenes.title: Seventy percent of stations met both PM₂.₅ standards
scenes.text: Across B.C., 40 of the 57 assessed stations met both the annual and 24-hour Canadian Ambient Air Quality Standards after applicable adjustments.
scenes.focus: Seven air zones and 57 assessed stations

scenes.label: Air zones
scenes.title: Only two air zones achieved the 24-hour standard
scenes.text: Coastal and Georgia Strait achieved both the annual and 24-hour standards. The zone colours show the management response associated with the annual assessment.

callout.label: Air-zone result
callout.detail: Coastal and Georgia Strait achieved both standards.

scenes.title: Station results reveal variation within air zones
scenes.text: The 57 station markers carry the Province's annual and 24-hour metrics and the corresponding management action. Select a station to inspect its assessment.

scenes.label: Data gaps
scenes.title: The Northwest air zone had no assessed station
scenes.text: No monitoring stations in the Northwest air zone had sufficient data for the 2022–2024 assessment, so the zone is shown in grey.
